tripcom.question: How do I book a hotel on Trip.com and earn its rewards?

guide.title_full: Book a Trip.com hotel and earn rewards
guide.summary: Sign in or join Trip.com, book an eligible hotel on its site or app, then complete your stay to earn Trip Coins.
guide.prerequisites: You need a Trip.com account and your hotel dates, destination, and guest details.

steps.name: Sign in or join
steps.text: Open Trip.com and sign in, or create an account. Members can earn Trip Coins from eligible hotel bookings.

steps.name: Search for a hotel
steps.text: Choose Hotels, enter your destination, check-in and check-out dates, and number of guests, then search. Compare the room price and details.

steps.name: Check the room conditions
steps.text: Before choosing a room, check its cancellation and change rules, what is included, and whether payment is due now or later. The booking is also subject to the hotel’s terms.

steps.name: Book and pay
steps.text: Select the room, enter the requested guest details, review the total and policies, then complete the booking on Trip.com. Keep the confirmation for your records.

steps.name: Complete your stay
steps.text: Trip.com’s stated hotel earning rate is 50 Trip Coins per US$100 (or equivalent) spent, before any applicable tier bonus. Coins are based on eligible final payment; the exact award is shown after booking. A fully cancelled hotel booking earns no coins, and previously awarded coins may be deducted.

steps.name: Check your rewards
steps.text: After the stay, check your Trip Coins balance in your Trip.com account. You can use coins toward eligible prepaid bookings; Trip.com says 100 Trip Coins is approximately US$1 in savings.

guide.disclaimer: Trip.com reward rates, eligibility, booking conditions, and exchange values can change; check the booking page and current rewards terms before paying.
cautions: Promotions or special booking types may be excluded from Trip Coins; check the offer’s terms.
Cancellation may reduce or remove rewards, so check the room’s cancellation policy before booking.

ibkr.question: How do I deposit money to IBKR from my Singapore bank account?

guide.title_full: Deposit money from a Singapore bank to IBKR
guide.summary: Create a deposit notification in IBKR, then use the instructions it gives you to send the money from your bank.
guide.prerequisites: You need an open IBKR account and access to Client Portal.

steps.name: Start a deposit
steps.text: Sign in to IBKR Client Portal. Choose Transfer & Pay > Transfer Funds > Make a Deposit, then select the account you want to fund.

steps.name: Choose the bank method
steps.text: Select the deposit currency and a method available to you. For a bank wire, select Bank Wire and enter your Singapore bank as the sending institution and the amount. The options shown may vary by account and currency.

steps.name: Get IBKR's instructions
steps.text: Submit the deposit notification and open the instructions IBKR provides. For a wire, use the routing details for that specific currency exactly as shown; IBKR says routing instructions vary by currency.

steps.name: Send the money from your bank
steps.text: In your Singapore bank's app or online banking, arrange the transfer using IBKR's instructions. A notification alone does not move money. Check your bank's fees and make sure the sending account is in your name; IBKR generally discourages and may reject third-party deposits.

steps.name: Check deposit status
steps.text: Return to Client Portal and check Transfer & Pay or transaction history for the deposit status. Credit timing depends on the method and the bank transfer.

guide.disclaimer: Funding methods, processing times and bank charges can change; check the instructions and fees shown by IBKR and your bank before sending.
cautions: Use the exact bank details IBKR provides for your chosen currency; do not rely on old instructions or details from someone else.
Ask your bank about transfer and intermediary-bank charges.

coinbase.question: How can I buy bitcoin on Coinbase?

guide.title_full: How to buy Bitcoin on Coinbase
guide.summary: Verify your Coinbase account, add an eligible payment method, then review and confirm a Bitcoin purchase.
guide.prerequisites: You need a verified Coinbase account and an eligible payment method linked to it.

steps.name: Add a payment method
steps.text: Sign in to Coinbase. Open Settings (or Profile & Settings in the app), choose Payment methods, then Add a payment method and follow the prompts. In Singapore, a debit card can be used to buy crypto; a bank account is for depositing or withdrawing cash.

steps.name: Start a Bitcoin purchase
steps.text: On the website, select Buy. In the app, select Buy & sell, then Buy. Choose Bitcoin and enter how much you want to spend.

steps.name: Review and confirm
steps.text: Choose or confirm your payment method, then select Review order. Check the total and any fees shown. If everything looks right, select Buy now.

legal.text: Coinbase says retail customers in Singapore cannot use Singapore-issued credit or charge cards to buy crypto; its Singapore payment options list debit cards for purchases. Coinbase Singapore is listed by MAS as a Major Payment Institution providing digital payment token services.

guide.disclaimer: Bitcoin prices can rise or fall sharply; this is general information, not financial advice.

cautions: Check the order preview for the final price and fees before confirming; minimum purchase amounts may vary.
Use only Coinbase’s official app or website, and never share your password or verification codes.

scooter.question: Can I ride my e-scooter on the footpath in Singapore?

guide.title_full: Can you ride an e-scooter on Singapore footpaths?
guide.summary: No. E-scooters are banned from footpaths; ride only on cycling paths.
guide.answer: No. In Singapore, e-scooters may be ridden only on cycling paths—not footpaths or roads. Riding on a footpath can lead to regulatory action, with a fine of up to S$2,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 3 months if convicted.

legal.text: The law prohibits riding an e-scooter on a footpath. If convicted, the penalty can be a fine of up to S$2,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 3 months.

guide.disclaimer: Rules and penalties may change; check LTA’s current guidance before riding.
cautions: Check that the path is designated as a cycling path; e-scooters are not allowed on roads either.

cpf.question: What is the difference between my CPF Ordinary Account and Special Account?

guide.title_full: Difference between your CPF OA and SA
guide.summary: The OA is mainly for housing and other eligible uses; the SA was for retirement savings and earned higher interest. Age 55 changes the SA rules.
guide.answer: Your Ordinary Account (OA) is mainly for housing, and can also be used for certain insurance, education and investments. Your Special Account (SA) was meant for retirement savings and generally earned a higher interest rate. For 1 October to 31 December 2026, CPF lists the basic rates as 2.5% for OA and 4% for SA. Rates are reviewed regularly, and extra interest may apply. Important if you are 55 or older: CPF closed the SA from 19 January 2025. Savings were transferred to your Retirement Account (up to the applicable Full Retirement Sum); any remaining SA savings went to your OA. If you are under 55, you can still have an SA.
guide.disclaimer: CPF rates and account rules can change; check your CPF account or contact CPF Board for details about your own balances.
